classification.difficultyReason: Identify the relevant whole population and decide whether each stated design covers all or only part. The qualified attempted-census cases require attention to design versus completed response, but the task remains direct application across familiar contexts.

content.prompt: Determine whether the intended survey design in each scenario is a census or a sample.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Everyone in the house getting to vote on which board game to play next.

answer.worked: Census. Everyone in the house is included, so the whole population is surveyed.

children.label: b
children.prompt: A scientist gathering 500g of soil to analyse land quality in the area.

answer.worked: Sample. The 500 g collected is only part of the soil in the area.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Every second shopper at a supermarket is asked if they like a product.

answer.worked: Sample. Asking every second shopper includes only part of the supermarket's shoppers.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A referendum where everyone in a country votes on a new law change.

answer.worked: Census. Under the stated scenario, everyone in the country votes, so the whole population is included.

children.label: e
children.prompt: A shop owner uses an automatic entrance counter to record every customer entry each day.

answer.worked: Census. The population is all customer entries that day, and every entry is counted.

inlines.text: A school conducts a survey to gather feedback on the quality of lunches.
They distribute the survey to every student in the school.

answer.worked: Census (intended design). Every student is offered the survey, so this is an attempted census. Complete response is not stated.

inlines.text: A polling agency conducts a survey to predict election outcomes.
They randomly select 5,000 voters across the country and gather their voting preferences.

answer.worked: Sample. The selected 5,000 voters are only part of the country's voters.

children.label: h
children.prompt: A company conducts a survey to gather feedback from all its employees about their satisfaction with the workplace environment.

answer.worked: Census. All the company's employees are included, so feedback is collected from the whole population.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Researchers conduct a survey to understand the prevalence of a specific health condition in a city. They randomly select households to participate in the survey.

answer.worked: Sample. Only selected households participate, so the survey covers part of the city's population.

children.label: j
children.prompt: A retail store sends out a survey to everyone who made a purchase in the past month to gauge their satisfaction with the store's services.

answer.worked: Census (intended design). Everyone who purchased in the past month is offered the survey, so this is an attempted census. Complete response is not stated.
